- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.

TITLE: Superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks for mask-free training of MVFA's segmentation adapters
SUMMARY: Refine label-restricted patch pseudo-masks by majority voting inside SLIC superpixels of the raw image before using them as Dice and Focal targets.
HYPOTHESIS: Superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks raise pseudo-mask Dice against true masks by at least 8 points over raw patch pseudo-masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and MVFA trained on them reaches at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities, versus at most 80% for raw patch pseudo-masks.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: target type for seg_adapters: true masks; raw patch pseudo-masks (problem rule); superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks with n_segments in {100, 200, 400}. Snapping: a superpixel is labelled anomalous if the area-weighted mean of the upsampled patch anomaly indicator inside it exceeds 0.5 and the image is labelled abnormal; normal images stay empty. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU vs. true masks, pixel AUROC and Dice of the trained model on held-out masked modalities, and boundary F1 (2-pixel tolerance).
RATIONALE: Patch-level pseudo-masks are 17x17 at 240 px, so each label covers a 14-pixel block and boundaries are wrong almost everywhere along a lesion; Dice supervision on such blocks teaches the adapters blocky maps. MLCA shows that raw-input detail matters for MVFA-style localisation. A cheap way to inject raw detail into the targets is to snap the patch pseudo-mask to image superpixels, so every pseudo-mask boundary follows an intensity edge.
METHOD: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute the problem's label-restricted patch rule (level-4 features, 99th percentile of normal-to-normal NN distances on source validation) giving a 17x17 binary map per abnormal image. 2) Upsample bilinearly to 240x240 to obtain an indicator a(x). 3) Run skimage.segmentation.slic(image, n_segments=200, compactness=10, channel_axis=None for grey images) on the 240x240 input. 4) For superpixel S: label = 1 if mean_{x in S} a(x) > 0.5. 5) Remove components smaller than 20 pixels. 6) dataset/medical_zero.py reads these masks for all datasets marked pseudo; train_zero.py keeps Focal + Dice unchanged. 7) n_segments selected on source validation by pseudo-mask Dice where masks exist in the source fold (never the target). Hyper-parameters otherwise as MVFA (lr 1e-3, 50 epochs).
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; raw patch pseudo-masks; snapped pseudo-masks (n_segments 100/200/400); masks removed from 1 and from all 3 masked sources. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU/boundary F1; trained-model pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if snapping does not raise pseudo-mask Dice by 8 points or the trained model's pixel AUROC is not higher than with raw patch pseudo-masks.

Parent 2:
TITLE: Graph-regularised pseudo-masks: CRF smoothing on the patch grid for mask-free MVFA training
SUMMARY: Clean label-restricted pseudo-masks with a fully connected CRF over patches whose unary term is the NN-distance score and whose pairwise term uses CLIP feature similarity and position.
HYPOTHESIS: CRF regularisation reduces isolated false-positive components in pseudo-masks by at least 50% and increases pseudo-mask Dice by at least 6 points, and MVFA trained on CRF-regularised pseudo-masks attains higher pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities than MVFA trained on raw pseudo-masks.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: target type: true masks; raw label-restricted pseudo-masks; CRF-regularised pseudo-masks with pairwise weight w in {1, 3, 5}. Unary: u_p = -log sigmoid((d_p - t_hi)/s), with s the std of normal-to-normal distances; pairwise: Potts with kernel w exp(-|x_p - x_q|^2/(2 theta_x^2) - (1 - cos(f_p, f_q))/theta_f), theta_x = 3 patches, theta_f = 0.1; mean-field inference, 10 iterations, on the 17x17 grid. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice, false-positive components per normal-appearing region, trained pixel AUROC and Dice.
RATIONALE: Label-restricted pseudo-masks contain isolated false positives (healthy but rare anatomy) and holes inside lesions. G-Anomaly shows that modelling the topology of image regions separates anomalies from normal texture. A pairwise graph model over patches (a dense CRF on the patch grid with feature and spatial affinities) can enforce that anomalous patches form coherent regions, removing isolated false positives and filling holes before the masks supervise MVFA.
METHOD: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute d_p and the label-restricted rule. 2) crf_refine.py: implement mean-field inference for a fully connected Potts CRF on 289 patches in PyTorch (dense 289x289 kernel, cheap). 3) Output q_p = P(anomalous); mask = q_p > 0.5, upsampled to 240 px; abnormal images only. 4) dataset/medical_zero.py loads the refined masks; train_zero.py unchanged. 5) w selected on source validation where source masks exist. Hyper-parameters: theta_x 3, theta_f 0.1, 10 iterations, MVFA training as in the paper.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; raw pseudo-masks; CRF with w in {1,3,5}; masks removed from 1 and 3 sources. Ablation: spatial-only kernel vs spatial+feature kernel. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice, isolated FP components, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if CRF masks do not reduce isolated components by half or if trained pixel AUROC does not improve.
